chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged regarding the flood of the valley of Mahzour that the upper part should withhold the water upon the lower part for the palm trees up to the two ankles, and for the crops up to the two shoe straps. Then the water should be sent to the lower part from that for the crops to the shoe strap, and for the palm trees to the ankle. Then the water should be sent to the lower part from that.
Ibn Abi Umeyr said: And Mahzour is a place of the valley.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on water distribution between upper and lower landowners in a valley?
ai.summary: This hadith, cited in *Al-Kafi*, records the Prophet’s judicial ruling (*qada*) in the valley of Mahzour, establishing a precise hydraulic hierarchy where upper landowners retain water to a specific depth (ankle-deep for palms, shoe-strap-deep for crops) before releasing it downstream. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle of preventing water hoarding (*kaf al-ma'*) and ensuring equitable distribution, serving as a foundational precedent for Islamic water rights jurisprudence (*fiqh al-miya*).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father altogether, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hakam Bin Ayman, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> judged regarding the flow of the water of the valley of Mahzour that the upper part can only withhold upon the lower part for the palm trees up to the two ankles, and for the cultivation up to the two shoe straps. Then he should send the water to the lower parts from that for the cultivation to the shoe-straps, and for the palm trees up to the two ankles. Then the water should be sent to the lower parts from that’.
Ibn Abu Umeyr (the narrator) said, ‘And Mahzour is a place of the valley’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from my from Hakam ibn Ayman from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘The Messenger of Allah once issued a judgment about the flood of the valley of Mahzur (name of a place). The amount of water that those of higher areas can hold is up to the anklebones for palm trees and up to one’s shoelaces for plantation. Thereafter water must be allowed for those below that; for plantation up to the shoelace and for the palm trees up to the anklebone, then allow water for those yet lower.’
Ibn abu ‘Umayr has made a statement that Mahrzur is the name of an area in the valley.”
